abstract: Verifies coastal archaeological site permits, artifact handling licenses, and advisory council approvals
system_message:
You are the Maritime Heritage Compliance Officer (MHC), responsible for verifying coastal archaeological site permits, artifact handling licenses, and advisory council approvals for candidate expedition bases.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Wet artifact desalination storage（CONSERV）
information_points.content:
MHC-CONSERV-4KW：Based on the onboard conservation lab survey, the Oceanic Discoverer Support Vessel provides a stabilized wet artifact tank capacity of 12 m3 in its chilled holding vats for timber and metal relic desalination.
MHC-CONSERV-GUD：An onboard conservation lab survey shows that the Pelagic Surveyor Semi-Submersible features a stabilized wet artifact tank capacity of 18 m3 across its chilled wet specimen holding vats for desalinating timber and metal relics.
MHC-CONSERV-TI5：The onboard conservation lab survey records that the Bathyal Sentinel Jackup Platform maintains a stabilized wet artifact tank capacity of 24 m3 in chilled wet specimen holding vats.

information_points.title: Verifies coastal archaeological site permits, artifact handling licenses, and advisory council approvals（PERMIT）
information_points.content:
MHC-PERMIT-8LV：Records from the state maritime archaeology regulatory registry confirm that the Oceanic Discoverer Support Vessel has maritime heritage preservation council authorization covering the shipwreck exploration permit area for excavation and non-destructive survey rights.
MHC-PERMIT-QLG：The state maritime archaeology regulatory registry indicates that the Bathyal Sentinel Jackup Platform does not have maritime heritage preservation council authorization for the shipwreck exploration permit area.
MHC-PERMIT-Z4R：According to the state maritime archaeology regulatory registry, the Pelagic Surveyor Semi-Submersible holds valid maritime heritage preservation council authorization for the shipwreck exploration permit area, granting excavation and non-destructive survey rights.
